words.gloss: only to those of such nature

literal: Crow without-concealing having-called eats; wealth-also to-those-of-such-nature-only exist.
translation: The crow does not hide its food, but calls out to its kind and eats with them. Prosperity abides only with people of such a nature.
modern: காக்கை தனக்குக் கிடைத்த உணவை மறைக்காமல் தன் சுற்றத்தைக் கூவி அழைத்துச் சேர்ந்து உண்ணும். செல்வம் அத்தகைய குணம் உடையவர்களிடமே நிலைத்திருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the natural behavior of the crow to illustrate the virtue of sharing with one's kindred. A crow does not hide its food ('கரவா'); instead, it calls out ('கரைந்து') to gather its flock before eating ('உண்ணும்'). The word 'ஆக்கம்' refers to wealth or prosperity, and 'அன்ன நீரார்க்கே' means 'only to those of such nature'. The poem teaches that lasting prosperity belongs only to those who, like the crow, openly share their good fortune with their relatives.
